rules.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance: source of income (including Section 8 and public benefits) as a protected category in tenant selection
rules.key_value: Source of income (incl. Section 8 and public benefits) protected; civil fines up to $300 per violation after Commission hearing

coverage.summary: Rental housing in Cambridge, except 2-family dwellings where the owner lives. Complements the state source-of-income protection in G.L. c. 151B, § 4(10); no preemption question is shown.
coverage.owner_conditions: Exemption for 2-family dwellings when the owner lives there.

rules.exemptions: 2-family dwellings when the owner lives there.
rules.effective_date_note: The documents give no enactment or effective date for ch. 14.04. The Commission was established in 1984, which is not necessarily the ordinance's date.
rules.quoted_span: Source of Income, includes Section 8 and public benefits
rules.review_note: The source is the Human Rights Commission's official FAQ page, not the ordinance text, so no section-level citation is available. The page does not address criminal-history, credit or eviction-record screening, or the timing of screening. The 2-family owner-occupied exemption is described only briefly. The $300 fine is described as a Commission remedy for violations generally, not specifically for this ordinance.
rules.source_notes: The protected-category list on D029 is stated jointly for the Cambridge Human Rights Ordinance (ch. 2.76) and the Fair Housing Ordinance (ch. 14.04). Housing discrimination is attributed to ch. 14.04. D029 lists the Tenants' Rights and Resources Notification Ordinance only as a link title; that ordinance is covered by the ch. 8.71 record.

rules.title: Cambridge Tenants Rights and Resources Notification Ordinance: Guide must be given at tenancy start and with a notice to quit or summary process
rules.requirement:
Owners, landlords and management companies must give tenants the City's Tenants Rights and Resources Guide at two points.
- At the start of a tenancy: when the tenant first signs a lease, enters a tenancy agreement, or tenders the first month's rent.
- When legal steps to terminate a tenancy are taken, such as a Notice to Quit or Summary Process. The Guide must be offered at the same time as the notice to quit or other action.

All tenants and lawful occupants, including tenants at will, must receive it. Renewals do not require it, and a signed tenant receipt is not required. The ordinance does not bar an eviction otherwise allowed by law. Violations may be fined $300 for each day's violation (§ 8.71.070).
rules.key_value: Guide required at tenancy start and with notice to quit or summary process; $300 fine per day of violation

unverifiable_exemptions: units in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is short-term substance abuse treatment or assistance
coverage.landlord_size_condition: Applies to all landlords, including an owner of a single rental unit in the building where the owner lives.
coverage.summary: Residential rental agreements in Cambridge, including single dwelling units and tenancies at will. Complements the state nonpayment notice-to-quit form required by G.L. c. 186, § 31.
coverage.other_conditions: Excludes rental units in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities, non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities, and Short Term Rental Units under Cambridge Zoning Ordinance Art. 4, § 4.60.

rules.exemptions: Rental units in a hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; units in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is short-term assistance, treatment or therapy for alcohol, drug or other substance abuse; Short Term Rental Units under Cambridge Zoning Ordinance Art. 4, § 4.60.
rules.effective_date_note: The documents do not state the effective date. The official FAQ page was posted 10/14/2020 and last modified 3/17/2025.
citation_aliases: Tenants Rights and Resources Notification Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The Ordinance also requires that a landlord provide the Guide to tenants when legal steps to terminate a tenancy are taken (ex. Notice to Quit or Summary Process).
rules.review_note: This is a tenant-rights notice rule tied to notices to quit, not a list of just causes; the documents show no Cambridge just-cause rule. The citation is at chapter level because the section containing the delivery requirement is not identified. Only § 8.71.030 (definitions) and § 8.71.070 (penalty) are named. The source is the official FAQ page, not the ordinance text.
